title_en: TTU154: Why Trend Following Isn't Crash Insurance ft. Philippe Jordan
title_zh: TTU154：为什么趋势跟踪不是崩盘保险——对话 CFM International 总裁 Philippe Jordan
subtitle_zh: CFM 总裁 Philippe Jordan 直言趋势跟踪只是0.5 Sharpe的分散工具，能分散却非崩盘保险。
description: TTU154: Why Trend Following Isn't Crash Insurance ft. Philippe Jordan

turns.en: [00:00:01] Philippe  There'sa period not so long ago, call it 10 years ago, where people were running around saying, trend is dead. And we found out that it isn’t. And the reality of trend is that it is a 0.5 Sharpe strategy. It does play a role in investor portfolios, that is valuable. It does diversify but it's
turns.zh: 不久前——大概就说10年前吧——有那么一段时间，人们到处嚷嚷'趋势已死'。结果我们发现事实并非如此。趋势（trend）的现实是：它是一个0.5夏普比率（Sharpe）的策略。它确实在投资者组合里发挥着有价值的作用，确实能分散风险，但它

turns.en: not going to pay for your crash. That's not what it does. [00:00:32] Intro  Welcometo Top Traders Unplugged. In markets success doesn’t come from predicting what happens next, it comes from being prepared for what you can’t predict. In each episode we go deep with some of the world’s most thoughtful minds in investing, economics,
turns.zh: 并不会为你的崩盘买单，那不是它的作用。欢迎收听 Top Traders Unplugged。在市场里，成功并不来自预测接下来会发生什么，而来自为你无法预测的东西做好准备。每一期节目，我们都会与全球投资、经济乃至更广领域里最善于思考的一些头脑深入交流，

turns.en: and beyond to understand how they think, how they prepare, and how they decide, and the experiences that shaped how they see the world. No noise, no short-cuts, just real conversations to help you think better and invest with confidence. [00:01:05] Niels  Philippe,if money flowing into a strategy helps create
turns.zh: 去理解他们如何思考、如何准备、如何决策，以及那些塑造了他们世界观的经历。没有噪音，没有捷径，只有真实的对话，帮助你更好地思考、更有信心地投资。Philippe，如果流入一个策略的资金本身有助于创造出

[00:01:21] Philippe  Ooh,well, that depends what frequency you're talking about. If you're talking about something that's operating at two to three or four days or a month in frequency, that would
turns.zh: 那些能吸引下一波投资者的回报，那么在这些资金流反转之前，我们怎么判断自己找到的是不是一个可持续的优势（edge）？哦，这得看你谈的是什么频率。如果你说的是那种在两三天、四天或者一个月频率上运作的东西，那

If you're talking about something that's operating over four months to six months in frequency and does have turnover as opposed to none, I would think that doesn't have much impact. turns.zh: 影响会相当大。如果你说的是那种在四到六个月频率上运作、并且确实有换手（turnover）而不是零换手的东西，我觉得影响就不大。如果你完全没有换手，那我认为影响会很大。是的，完全同意。

turns.en: Well, today, Alan and I are joined by Philippe Jordan, president of CFM International. And for those who may be newer to the show, CFM is one of the leading quantitative investment firms in Europe and in the world, with about 36 billion in assets under management. Philippe, before we get into how CFM invests, I'd
turns.zh: 今天，Alan 和我请到了 CFM International 的总裁 Philippe Jordan。对于刚接触本节目的听众，CFM 是欧洲乃至全球领先的量化投资公司之一，管理资产规模约360亿。Philippe，在我们深入探讨 CFM 如何投资之前，我

turns.en: like to understand how you came to see the market this way. You joined CFM in 2005. What brought you there? And which experiences, early in your career, had most shaped you to decide that CFM would be a good opportunity for you? [00:02:33] Philippe  Goodmorning, Niels. Thanks for having me. Hi, Alan. I'm delighted to meet you
turns.zh: 想先了解你是怎么形成如今这种市场观的。你在2005年加入 CFM。是什么把你带到那里的？在你职业生涯早期，哪些经历最深刻地塑造了你，让你认定 CFM 会是一个好机会？早上好，Niels，谢谢你们邀请我。你好，Alan，很高兴认识你，

turns.en: and have this conversation. Well, I have to dig back deep into my memory for this. Yeah, I joined in ‘05, but I started doing business with CFM in ‘91. So, I was one of CFM's brokers and I became a friend, a fast friend of Jean-Pierre Aguilar, the founder, who was a terrific guy, who unfortunately left us in a tragic
turns.zh: 也很高兴有这次对话。这个我得好好翻一翻记忆深处了。是的，我2005年加入，但1991年就开始和 CFM 做生意了。当时我是 CFM 的经纪商之一，后来成了创始人 Jean-Pierre Aguilar 的朋友，而且是很快结下的挚友。他是个极棒的人，可惜在一场悲剧性的

turns.en: accident over a decade ago, now, doing something that he loved, which is flying airplanes that don't have engines, otherwise known as gliders. He had a real quality to him in terms of charisma and entrepreneurship. And his vision, which I came to share ultimately was, look, there has to be a better way to trade and invest in
turns.zh: 事故中离开了我们——那已经是十多年前的如今了。他当时正在做自己热爱的事：驾驶没有引擎的飞机，也就是滑翔机（gliders）。他身上有一种真正的特质，无论是个人魅力还是创业精神。而他的愿景——我最终也认同了——是：瞧，一定有一种更好的方式来交易和投资

turns.en: markets than reading newspapers and developing narratives. And that should consist in using data. And back in those days, data was a very simple form of data. It was price-based data and computers to analyze that data, extract the signal, and then executed faithfully because we didn’t have electronic systems. So,
turns.zh: 市场，而不是靠读报纸、编叙事。那应该建立在运用数据之上。而在当年，数据是非常简单的形式——基于价格的数据，再用计算机去分析这些数据、提取信号，然后忠实执行，因为我们那时还没有电子化系统。所以，

turns.en: I execute all these signals manually in the markets on behalf of CFM. That approach had merit, but it also had a lot of drawbacks. Trend following is an interesting strategy. It has a very robust Sharpe, but it doesn't have a Sharpe of 1.0. It has a Sharpe, over the long term, of probably 0.5, which, over the long
turns.zh: 我就代表 CFM 在市场里手动执行所有这些信号。那种做法有其价值，但也有很多缺点。趋势跟踪（trend following）是个很有意思的策略。它有一个非常稳健的夏普比率，但达不到1.0。它的长期夏普比率大概是0.5，而放在长期

turns.en: term, is very good. That's actually better than the stock market over the long term (not the stock market in the last 10 years or 20, but the long, long term). And then Jean-Pierre had this sort of increased vision which is, well, yeah, I need something else to sit beside this trend following strategy. And I need to
turns.zh: 来看，这已经非常好了。实际上比股市的长期表现还要好（不是指过去10年、20年的股市，而是非常非常长期的）。后来 Jean-Pierre 有了更进一步的想法：嗯，我需要别的东西来和这个趋势跟踪策略并列，而我需要

turns.en: work with scientists that are going to allow me to gain insight into things like statistical arbitrage, volatility, arbitrage, any number of other techniques that are essentially extracting data using a scientific framework and then executing it systematically. Systematically, still, in the ‘90s, means with hands, telephones,
turns.zh: 和科学家们合作，让我能洞察诸如统计套利（statistical arbitrage）、波动率套利（volatility arbitrage）以及无数其他技术——它们本质上都是用一套科学框架去提取数据，然后系统化地执行。而在90年代，所谓'系统化'仍然意味着靠双手、电话、

turns.en: faxes, it's still very manual. We were working on spinning out… not spinning out… but seeding a number
turns.zh: 传真，非常手工化。我作为经纪商跟随了这一演变五六年，之后又作为母基金（fund of fund）经理去考察 CFM，再到 Credit Suisse 时我做分拆（spin out）——把像 Alan Howard 和 CQS 这样的人分拆出来。我们当时在做分拆……不是分拆……而是为一系列

And we had crossed what I call the threshold of velocity for that business because, prior to 2000, that business was executed by people like
turns.zh: 策略在 CFM 提供种子资金（seeding），合作方是 Credit Suisse Capital。但那没能成行，因为 Credit Suisse——不愧是 Credit Suisse——很不稳定。所以那个委托很遗憾地化为乌有。而那时我们已经跨过了我所谓的这项业务的'速度门槛'，因为在2000年以前，这项业务是由像

turns.en: me, manually. Post 2000, this business went fully electronic. So, people like me were out of the picture. And all of a sudden, this business is being implemented by execution algos. And so, it becomes much more scalable. You're able to trade at many different frequencies that were not accessible when people like me were executing these
turns.zh: 我这样的人手工执行的。2000年以后，这项业务完全电子化了。于是，像我这样的人就被淘汰出局。突然间，这项业务开始由执行算法（execution algos）来实施，因此它变得可扩展得多。你能在很多不同的频率上交易，而这些频率在像我这样的人手工执行这些

turns.en: signals for people like Jean-Pierre. And finally, Jean-Pierre ran two businesses. He had a hedge fund and he had a company that designed systems on behalf of banks, middle office systems, option systems. And there was some compatibility between the two businesses. There were some interesting synergies because there were some
turns.zh: 信号（替 Jean-Pierre 那样的人）时是无法触及的。最后，Jean-Pierre 经营着两块业务：一家对冲基金，以及一家替银行设计系统的公司——中台系统、期权系统。这两块业务之间有一定的兼容性，也有一些有意思的协同效应，因为这边有一些

turns.en: engineers over here that knew how to build systems and a hedge fund over here. But there was also a duality of purpose, and I didn't really like that. And he called me one day and he said, well, I'm selling the engineering business and I'm going to focus entirely on the hedge fund business. And that for me, in
turns.zh: 懂得如何搭建系统的工程师，那边有一家对冲基金。但同时也存在目标上的二元性，这一点我不太喜欢。有一天他给我打电话说：嗯，我要把工程业务卖掉，全身心专注于对冲基金业务。对我而言，这一点，再加上

turns.en: combination with all the other things, made CFM, in my view, a very compelling firm for the future. And I wanted to join that and help build it. [00:07:34] Niels  Yeah,just out of curiosity, obviously, I mean, you and I, and Alan for that matter, we're all there in the ‘80s and the ‘90s before things got systematic, electronic,
turns.zh: 其他所有这些因素，让 CFM 在我看来成为一家对未来非常有吸引力的公司。我想加入它，帮助把它建立起来。是的，纯粹出于好奇——显然，你和我，还有 Alan，我们都经历过80年代、90年代，那时一切还没有变得系统化、电子化，

turns.en: and so on, and so forth. Was there something in particular, you remember, that you kind of had to unlearn when you started working with the scientists back then about how markets work or something that we had all come to believe, but maybe we realized maybe it's not so. [00:08:06] Philippe   Iwouldsay that there was
turns.zh: 诸如此类。你还记不记得，当年你开始和那些科学家共事时，有没有什么关于市场如何运作的东西是你不得不'忘掉'（unlearn）的？或者是我们大家都曾深信不疑、但后来也许意识到未必如此的东西？我想说的是，当时确实有

turns.en: a need for a point of convergence, and I'll explain that. If you're viewing the world through the prism of statistics, and Gaussian distributions ,and fat tails, etc., what happens, happens (to a certain extent), and you have to live with it. The path to deal with the negative outcomes is to further diversify
turns.zh: 一种对'汇合点'（point of convergence）的需要，我来解释一下。如果你透过统计学的棱镜来看世界——高斯分布（Gaussian distributions）、肥尾（fat tails）等等——那么该发生的就会发生（在某种程度上），你必须接受它。应对负面结果的路径，就是尽可能地进一步分散你的

turns.en: your book as much as you can, which is a very rational approach and it makes sense. However, from time to time, history does actually happen, and the outcomes can be absolutely extreme, and you need to do things that are not statistically driven and are not systematic. And I had to evolve my view from, ‘well, you need
turns.zh: 账本（book），这是非常理性的做法，也讲得通。然而，历史时不时地真的会发生，结果可能极端到无以复加，这时你就需要做一些不由统计驱动、也不系统化的事情。我不得不让自己的观点演变：从'嗯，你需要

turns.en: to develop an intuition about what your risk is, do something about it all the time’ to, ‘no, most of the time you don't if you have a properly diversified book, in terms of strategies per correlations, tail structure, and something that's fairly well ballaced.’ And then they had to come a bit to me, which is, well, sometimes really
turns.zh: 培养一种对自身风险的直觉，并且时时刻刻去应对它'，演变为'不，如果你的账本在策略、相关性、尾部结构上都充分分散、并且相当均衡，那么大多数时候你并不需要那样做'。然后他们也得朝我这边靠一点，也就是：嗯，有时候确实

turns.en: bad things do happen that have high impact that can kill you when you're in this particular business, and that can be counterparty failure, that can be airplanes that crash into buildings in New York City and suspend trading for a week. There are things… In the case of airplanes crashing into buildings, you can do things
turns.zh: 会发生一些影响巨大、能要你命的坏事——尤其是当你身处这一行时。那可能是交易对手违约（counterparty failure），也可能是飞机撞进纽约的大楼、导致交易停摆一周。有些事情……就飞机撞楼这种情况，你能做的事情是

turns.en: post not pre. But in the case of counterparty management, there's things that you can do pre that matter and will settle outcomes favorably. In the case of crowding, also, the first case of crowding in our business, that I remember vividly, is the quant crunch of ’07, in August of ‘07. That was quite clear to me that
turns.zh: 事后而非事前的。但在交易对手管理（counterparty management）方面，有些事你可以在事前做，而且很关键，能让结果朝着有利的方向落定。拥挤交易（crowding）也是一样。我还清晰记得的、我们这行第一次拥挤交易案例，就是2007年的'量化地震'（quant crunch），发生在2007年8月。当时我非常清楚，

turns.en: it was occurring. Meaning if you go back to July of ‘07, you're in the first phases of the big deleveraging of mortgage books by Wall Street banks. And you're in the first phase… that's ‘07 or ’08? Help me here. [00:10:51] Alan  Itwould be ’07, yes. [00:10:52] Philippe  It's‘07. Yeah, it is. ‘07. It’s so long ago. So, in
turns.zh: 它正在发生。也就是说，如果你回到2007年7月，你正处在华尔街各大银行对抵押贷款账本大去杠杆的最初阶段。你就处在最初阶段……那是2007还是2008？帮我一下。是2007年，对。是2007年。是啊，是2007年，好久以前了。所以，在

turns.en: July, we're going through this mortgage deleveraging of bank balance sheets and it gets acute. Right? And when that happens, people that run trading rooms tend to run around the trading room and want balance sheet back because at one stage they can no longer liquidate what they're liquidating because everybody's trying to liquidate,
turns.zh: 7月，我们正经历银行资产负债表的这场抵押贷款去杠杆，而且变得非常尖锐。对吧？当这种情况发生时，管理交易台（trading room）的人往往会绕着交易台跑，想要收回资产负债表额度，因为到了某个阶段，他们已经无法平仓手头的头寸了——因为每个人都在试图平仓，

turns.en: but they do need balance sheet. And if you run around the trading room, you go see the macro guy and you say, well, how much balance sheet do you have on? He might have half a billion dollars worth of directional risk with a lot of VaR, but not a lot of balance sheet. And you keep running through your departments,
turns.zh: 但他们确实需要资产负债表额度。于是你绕着交易台跑，去找做宏观的那个人说：嗯，你占用了多少资产负债表额度？他可能有5亿美元的方向性风险，VaR 很高，但占用的资产负债表并不多。然后你继续跑遍你的各个部门，

turns.en: you're going to meet Mr. Fixed Income Relative Value, that has a lot. And you're going to meet Mr. Statistical Arbitrage, that has a lot. And you're going to ask them for balance sheet back, which will produce a negative effect on portfolios that are highly diversified but are long and short equities. And at first cut, people
turns.zh: 你会遇到'固定收益相对价值'先生，他占用很多；你还会遇到'统计套利'先生，他也占用很多。然后你会向他们要回资产负债表额度，这会对那些高度分散、但做多又做空股票的组合产生负面影响。而一开始，那些

turns.en: that run businesses statistically will look at any drop as an opportunity to add risk until their own risk systems saturate and you get a negative feedback loop that gets amplified with every day that goes through. And we made the decision collectively, but I was certainly a big proponent of it,
turns.zh: 以统计方式经营业务的人，会把任何下跌都看作是加仓风险的机会，直到他们自己的风险系统饱和，然后你就得到一个负反馈循环，而且每过一天都被放大一次。我们集体做出了这个决定，但我当然是它的大力倡导者，

turns.en: of getting out of the way. Of course, that's only half the equation. You get out of the way, that's great. But then do you get back in September fast enough to make up for how quickly positions are being rebuilt and P&L is being rebuilt, which we did, but it wasn't perfect. But that's to illustrate the fact that we now have
turns.zh: 那就是'让路'（get out of the way）。当然，这只是等式的一半。你让开了路，很好。但接下来，你在9月能不能足够快地重新进场，以弥补头寸和损益（P&L）重建的速度？我们做到了，但并不完美。但这正说明了这样一个事实：我们现在有了

turns.en: a point of convergence where we, today, have a group of, I think it's 11 people that meet every two weeks to discuss potential unknown unknowns, terrorists that can affect our business, our portfolio, our business, every part of our business; operationally, portfolio wise, regulatory wise, all sorts of dimensions away from simply
turns.zh: 一个汇合点。今天，我们有一个小组——我想是11个人——每两周开一次会，讨论潜在的'未知的未知'（unknown unknowns），讨论那些可能影响我们业务、我们组合、我们生意每一个部分的恐怖主义威胁：运营层面、组合层面、监管层面，各种维度，而不仅仅是

turns.zh: 组合风险。你提到 CFM 起步于1991年。那首先意味着——恭喜35周年，这是很大的成就。如今，相比你们起家的那个管理期货（managed futures）领域，你们运营的策略要宽泛得多。你会说，

turns.zh: 在这35年里，哪些决定最改变了公司的方向？我又要带你回到我关于趋势跟踪的那句话了。公司1991年起步，在91、92、93年像火箭一样腾飞，然后到了94年——我不知道你记不记得——当时有一样

[00:14:31] Philippe  Well,that event was very painful for CFM and
turns.zh: 东西，叫……是 Tesobonos 吗？那是1994年的墨西哥固定收益危机。嗯。它引发了逃向优质资产（flight to quality）、涌入美国国债，然后是一轮大幅降息周期，紧接在之前的大幅升息周期之后。没错。嗯，那次事件对 CFM 和它的

turns.zh: 趋势业务来说都非常痛苦。而 Jean-Pierre 有那份洞察力和创业精神，他说：嗯，我需要找到其他策略，它们共享这套科学框架和对待数据的方式，但我需要的其他策略要与这个策略从根本上不相关（decorrelated）。我需要开始在趋势之外搭建积木，以
